data.description:
## Symptom

`provision_toolchain` in `tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` (around `:151`) runs its fast-path `_satisfied()`
check **before** taking the `flock`, and treats the bundle as ready on mere existence. A worker can
therefore observe a partially-written `node_modules`/`dist`, conclude provisioning is done, return
early, and run tests against a bundle another worker is still writing.

Flagged as an advisory by the LLM reviewer on Gerrit change 2600 patchset 3, and judged a real defect
rather than a style note by the implementing agent.

## Why it was not fixed in 2600

Change 2600 is the fix for bug `9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091`, which was failing ~46% of CI runs repo-wide and
blocking every open change. Pushing a further patchset would have reset its `LLM-Review +1` and cost
another full review plus CI cycle on the change that was unblocking the repository. The deliberate
call was to land 2600 and track this separately.

**This is not a regression introduced by 2600.** Before that change there was no lock at all and
workers raced freely; 2600 narrowed the window substantially. This ticket closes the remainder.

## Fix shape

Drop the unlocked fast path and perform the `_satisfied()` check **inside** the lock. An `flock` on a
local file costs microseconds and is taken a handful of times per run, so the fast path buys
negligible time while creating the window.

## Acceptance criteria

All deterministic and verifiable in a single run — no "run it a few times and see".

1. A test demonstrates the race deterministically **before** the fix: one worker is made to observe
   the partially-written state (e.g. hold the lock while a bundle is half-created, or stub the
   filesystem state the fast path inspects) and is shown returning early. RED first — a race
   asserted only by repetition is not a reproduction.
2. After the fix, the same test shows the second worker blocking on the lock and observing only a
   complete bundle.
3. The existing provisioning behaviour is unchanged for the uncontended case: `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py`
   still passes in full, and a cold single-worker run still provisions exactly once.
4. **Defect-seeded**: restoring the unlocked fast path makes AC1's test fail again. Demonstrated by
   mutation, then reverted.
5. No new mechanism is registered — this should be a movement of an existing check, not new
   machinery. Verify with `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` **and** `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py`
   (the latter is not covered by `make lint`).

## Note

`tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` and its lock were introduced by change 2600; read that change first for the
surrounding design, including why provisioning moved out of the fixture into
`pytest_collection_modifyitems` and why a failed pre-provision must degrade to the in-fixture path
rather than fail the step.
data.title: e2e toolchain provisioning has an unlocked fast path: a worker can run against a bundle another worker is still writing
